summary.text: A 66-year-old man presented with recurrent perianal abscesses over a 12-month period. His history included perianal trauma from sitting on broken glass in childhood, vascular dementia, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, atrial fibrillation and gout. He was a former smoker with no known family history of malignancy and no known history of perianal warts, sexually transmitted disease, immune deficiency, inflammatory dermatoses or arsenic exposure.

Ultrasound fine needle aspiration of the abscess yielded 15 cc of purulent material; Gram stain and culture were negative and cytology showed atypical squamous cells. The postdrainage differential diagnosis included squamous cell carcinoma, cyst, condyloma or large abscess. Because of the cytology he was referred to a colorectal surgeon, but the appointment was delayed 2 months and the mass increased in size, prompting concern for a fistula.

Rectal examination revealed a fluctuant mass in the left lateral quadrant without external fistulas. The abscess was drained surgically, yielding purulent fluid with improvement in pain, and the culture showed no microbial growth. An examination under anesthesia less than one month later showed an external sinus tract into the mass but no clear fistula to the anal canal.

The mass was excised completely and the defect closed primarily. The specimen contained a 3.0 cm nodule; microscopy showed a nodular tumor with peripheral palisading, mucin and dark-brown pigment, immunohistochemistry was positive for CK7, CK903 and Ber-EP4 and negative for HMB45 and MITF, and the margins were more than 1 mm from the tumor. The authors describe a large pigmented basal cell carcinoma arising in a non-sun-exposed area.

At one-month follow-up the wound had completely healed. No further adjuvant therapy was performed except periodic and dermatologic surveillance. At two-year follow-up there had been no recurrence or complications, and a figure shows the healed incision site at 10 months postoperatively.

Figure 3
(a) A nodular, well-circumscribed basophilic tumor involved the dermis and displayed areas of cystic architecture (arrows). (b) The tumor cells were basaloid, small, hyperchromatic, and mostly uniform. Nodules exhibited peripheral palisading cells and retraction artifact (arrows). (c) Islands of mucin (arrows) were present within the tumor. (d) Some tumor nodules exhibited dark-brown pigment centrally. (e) The pigment was coarse and acellular. (f) Desmoplastic stroma harboring cholesterol clefts (arrows) and clumps of pigment was seen in nodule centers. (a–f) Hematoxylin and eosin: (a) 20x, (b) 40x, (c) 100x, (d) 40x, (e) 200x, and (f) 100x.
